summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the sunnah of delaying Isha prayer to the end of the first third or half of the night, explaining that the Prophet Muhammad would sometimes pray very late when the city became dark and people fell asleep waiting in the masjid. Sh. Ali Mashhour clarifies that the Prophet discouraged sleeping before Isha and engaging in extended conversations after Fajr, though he exempts necessary matters like seeking knowledge and important discussions. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that those waiting in the masjid for prayer are considered in a state of worship, and provides narrations from Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim to support these points.

catchy_title: Why did the Prophet delay Isha until the city slept?
